page: Amazon Web Services c6in.metal is a bare-metal compute-optimized server powered by Intel Xeon 8375C processors built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance delivers 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores operating at 3.5 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. System memory consists of 256 GB of DDR4 clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a compute-aligned ratio of 2 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX-512 with Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI), hardware-accelerated encryption extensions (AES, VAES, SHA_NI), and hardware-level memory encryption through Intel TME.

Hardware connectivity is characterized by a high-throughput 200 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, specifically designed for network-intensive and clustered environments. The c6in.metal configuration does not include local disk storage, requiring external network-attached block storage for persistent data. It also omits dedicated GPU accelerators, relying entirely on host CPU processing.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier multi-threaded compute and instruction performance, reflected in a PassMark CPU score of 87,698.18, a multi-core stress-ng rating of 124,964.56, and superior marks in ray tracing and image processing. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 335.16 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput measures 69.88 GB/sec alongside 112.35 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, single-threaded metrics remain within average bands across Geekbench and compression tasks, highlighting that overall compute efficiency is maximized through dense parallel execution.

Due to its high core density, extensive network pipe, and direct hardware access without hypervisor overhead, c6in.metal is positioned for distributed high-performance computing (HPC), network virtualization, parallel software compilation, static asset delivery, and compute-intensive batch workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services c6in.metal is a bare-metal compute-optimized server driven by 64-core Intel Xeon 8375C processors running at 3.5 GHz, providing 128 dedicated vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture. The platform features 256 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, matching a compute-centric 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It includes no local storage or discrete GPUs, relying on remote block storage while exposing a massive 200 Gbps baseline network capacity. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier multi-core computing, vector processing, and cryptography performance, complemented by 335.16 GB/sec in large-block uncached memory read bandwidth and 69.88 GB/sec in web throughput. The bare-metal design avoids virtualization latency, making the instance well structured for distributed compute clusters, parallel software compilation, network appliances, and intensive batch processing pipelines.
